panels.title: Role
panels.description: postgresql.recovery.active from the pack. Not a configured label: a promoted standby changes this value.

panels.title: Streaming
panels.description: 1 when pg_stat_wal_receiver reports streaming. Always 0 on a primary; the alert only applies to a standby.

panels.title: Heartbeat
panels.description: 1 whenever the pack heartbeat query succeeded. No data means the target is silent (PostgresTargetAbsent).

panels.title: Collector self-metric
panels.description: otelcol_process_uptime; no data means the Collector is gone (CollectorAbsent).

panels.title: Replay backlog
panels.description: Received minus replayed WAL on a standby. The dashed line is the limit of PostgresReplayBacklog: obenhub.postgresql.replay_backlog.limit, 256 MiB when the lab records none.

panels.title: Oldest snapshot age
panels.description: Age of the oldest client transaction holding a snapshot or xid. The dashed line is the limit of PostgresSnapshotHeldTooLong: obenhub.postgresql.snapshot_age.limit, 1800 s when the lab records none.

panels.title: Oldest xmin held (transactions)
panels.description: Largest age() of any xmin or xid held by a backend (walsender feedback included), a replication slot (xmin, catalog_xmin) or a prepared transaction. What the snapshot age panel cannot show: slots and standby feedback have no timestamp. No alert reads it yet.

panels.title: Client connections vs capacity

targets.expr: postgresql.client_connection.limit{obenhub.cluster.name="$cluster", service.instance.id="$instance"} * on() group_left() (obenhub.postgresql.connection_saturation.limit{severity="warning"} or on() vector(0.85))

panels.description: Client backends against max_connections minus superuser and reserved slots.

panels.title: Commits and rollbacks per second
panels.description: postgresqlreceiver sums are cumulative counters, so these are rate() over them, summed over databases.

panels.title: Replication slots: WAL retained
panels.description: retained_wal is current LSN minus restart_lsn, all slots on all nodes, not filtered by the instance variable. PostgresReplicationSlotRetainingWAL fires above obenhub.postgresql.slot_retained_wal.limit (8 GiB by default) on a primary; the logical slots have their own panel in the Logical replication row.

panels.title: Replication slots: active and inactive time
panels.description: active is 1 while a process streams from the slot; postgresql.replication_slot.inactive_age counts from pg_replication_slots.inactive_since. The standby slot standby1 is physical and not covered by the alert.

panels.title: WAL archiving: files waiting, failing, failures
panels.description: pg_stat_archiver and the .ready files in pg_wal/archive_status. Alerts: PostgresArchivingFailing (failing = 1 for 1 minute) and PostgresArchiveBacklog (more than 8 files waiting for 2 minutes).

panels.title: Transaction-id age (share of the wraparound limit)
panels.description: age(datfrozenxid) and mxid_age(datminmxid) of the oldest database, divided by 2^31 as PostgresTransactionIdWraparound does (the alert takes every database separately). The dashed lines are its tiers, obenhub.postgresql.wraparound_ratio.limit by severity (0.5 and 0.75 when the lab records none), each held for 5 minutes, primary only. Autovacuum keeps the figure far below that in the labs.

panels.title: Idle in transaction: oldest session
panels.description: Seconds the longest-idle session has been idle in a transaction (0 when there is none). The dashed lines are the PostgresIdleInTransaction tiers, obenhub.postgresql.idle_in_transaction_age.limit by severity (300 s and 1800 s when the lab records none), each held for 45 s.

panels.title: Locks: oldest wait and waiting sessions
panels.description: The longest wait for a lock (seconds) and the number of sessions waiting (right axis). The dashed line is the limit of PostgresBlockedSessions: obenhub.postgresql.lock_wait_age.limit, 120 s when the lab records none, held for 30 s. A deadlock does not show here for long: PostgreSQL aborts one session after deadlock_timeout.

panels.title: Deadlocks in the last 5 minutes
panels.description: Deadlocks detected per database over a sliding 5 minutes: last minus first sample, the expression of PostgresDeadlocks (any value above 0 fires). Only the databases the Collector receiver lists are counted.

panels.title: Checkpoints in the last 5 minutes
panels.description: Checkpoints per type over a sliding 5 minutes, as in PostgresCheckpointsRequested: more requested than the dashed line (obenhub.postgresql.requested_checkpoints.limit, 3 when the lab records none) for 1 minute fires. Requested ones come from WAL reaching max_wal_size, CHECKPOINT, base backups and promotion; scheduled ones from checkpoint_timeout. A standby counts restartpoints, so it stays near 0.

panels.title: Sessions by wait event type
panels.description: Client sessions at each scrape grouped by wait_event_type of pg_stat_activity, stacked. 'none' is a session that is not waiting (running, or idle without a wait event). One scan of pg_stat_activity, the scraping backend excluded; a type with no session at a scrape has no point.

panels.title: Sessions by wait event (top 10)

targets.expr: topk_max(10, sum by (postgresql.wait_event.type, postgresql.wait_event.name) (postgresql.client_session.count{obenhub.cluster.name="$cluster", service.instance.id="$instance", postgresql.wait_event.name!="none"}))

panels.description: The ten wait events with the most sessions at their peak in the selected range (topk_max), sessions that are not waiting left out. Wait event names are PostgreSQL's (pg_stat_activity, wait events); the series set is bounded by that vocabulary, not by the workload.

panels.title: Statements: execution time per second
panels.description: pg_stat_statements gauges: the sum of the statements still in the view, which falls when entries are evicted, so the panels use deriv() (not rate(), which reads a fall as a counter reset and spikes) and clamp negative values to 0. A rate under-reports while statements are being evicted (PostgresStatementsEvicted). Seconds of statement execution time per second, per database; above 1 means more than one session's worth of work.

panels.title: Statements: calls per second
panels.description: pg_stat_statements gauges: the sum of the statements still in the view, which falls when entries are evicted, so the panels use deriv() (not rate(), which reads a fall as a counter reset and spikes) and clamp negative values to 0. A rate under-reports while statements are being evicted (PostgresStatementsEvicted). Statement executions per second, per database.

panels.title: Statements: temp blocks written per second
panels.description: pg_stat_statements gauges: the sum of the statements still in the view, which falls when entries are evicted, so the panels use deriv() (not rate(), which reads a fall as a counter reset and spikes) and clamp negative values to 0. A rate under-reports while statements are being evicted (PostgresStatementsEvicted). Blocks of temporary files written per second (sorts, hashes and so on that did not fit in work_mem), per database.

panels.title: Statements evicted in the last 5 minutes
panels.description: Rise of pg_stat_statements_info.dealloc over a sliding 5 minutes: last minus first sample, the expression of PostgresStatementsEvicted (any value above 0 fires).

panels.title: Autovacuum (slow tier, every 5 minutes; labs: slice1, stage3, pgha, k8s)
Autovacuum backlog: tables past their threshold
panels.description: Tables whose dead tuples exceed autovacuum_vacuum_threshold plus autovacuum_vacuum_scale_factor times reltuples and that no vacuum finished on in the last three autovacuum_naptime intervals (storage parameters honoured, tables with autovacuum disabled left out; a small table autovacuum vacuums every round is not counted although it crosses its threshold between rounds); PostgresAutovacuumBacklog fires when it stays above 0 for 15 minutes. Slow tier: collected every 5 minutes, so the panel reads last_over_time over 10 minutes (two collections) and the line is a step; one series per database the slow-tier receiver reads (packs/postgresql/README.md, Slow tier); no series on a standby.

panels.title: Tables with autovacuum disabled
panels.description: Tables with the storage parameter autovacuum_enabled false; PostgresAutovacuumTableDisabled fires when it stays above 0 for 15 minutes. Slow tier: collected every 5 minutes, so the panel reads last_over_time over 10 minutes (two collections) and the line is a step; one series per database the slow-tier receiver reads (packs/postgresql/README.md, Slow tier); no series on a standby.

panels.title: Settings: autovacuum and track_counts (1 = on)
panels.description: 1 when the setting is on; PostgresAutovacuumOff fires when either is 0 for 5 minutes. Slow tier: collected every 5 minutes, so the panel reads last_over_time over 10 minutes (two collections) and the line is a step; one series per database the slow-tier receiver reads (packs/postgresql/README.md, Slow tier); no series on a standby.

panels.title: Logical replication (labs with a subscriber: slice1)
Subscription: enabled and apply worker
panels.description: From pg_subscription and pg_stat_subscription on the subscriber. A disabled subscription is expected to have no worker.

panels.title: Subscription: age of last message
panels.description: pg_stat_subscription.last_msg_receipt_time of the apply worker; 0 while there is no worker. A healthy idle subscription peaks near 30 s.

panels.title: Subscription: apply errors, sync errors, conflicts
panels.description: Cumulative counters from pg_stat_subscription_stats. An insert_exists conflict raises apply errors about every 5 s until it is resolved; conflict types at zero are hidden.

panels.title: Logical slots: unconfirmed WAL
panels.description: unconfirmed_wal (logical slots) is current LSN minus confirmed_flush_lsn. The dashed line is the PostgresLogicalSlotStalled limit, obenhub.postgresql.logical_slot_unconfirmed_wal.limit (4 GiB by default).

panels.title: PgBouncer: clients active and waiting
panels.description: SHOW POOLS cl_active and cl_waiting through the Collector. The console pool (database pgbouncer) is always listed; pools of other databases appear with their first client. Not filtered by the instance variable: PgBouncer is its own target.

panels.title: PgBouncer: server connections vs pool size
panels.description: SHOW POOLS sv_active, sv_idle and sv_used against SHOW DATABASES pool_size. Active at pool_size means the next client queues.

panels.title: PgBouncer: oldest waiting client
panels.description: SHOW POOLS maxwait plus maxwait_us (pgbouncer.pool.oldest_wait_age plus pgbouncer.pool.oldest_wait_subsecond_age, both in seconds). PgbouncerClientsWaiting fires above 5 s for 1 m.

panels.title: PgBouncer: client connections vs max_client_conn
panels.description: SHOW LISTS used_clients against the max_client_conn setting (SHOW CONFIG). used_clients includes the console connections, which count towards the limit but are never refused; a client beyond the limit is refused and counted nowhere. Not filtered by the instance variable: PgBouncer is its own target.

panels.title: PgBouncer: average wait and query time
panels.description: Data only during a scenario or other PgBouncer traffic. SHOW STATS totals as rate ratios, in seconds: wait per server assignment and server time per query. Wait time is counted only when a wait ends in an assignment. Query time includes the wait (PgBouncer starts timing when the query arrives, not when a server is assigned). A database with no traffic in the window has no point. Not filtered by the instance variable: PgBouncer is its own target.

panels.title: Last backup age
panels.description: Seconds since the last completed backup of any kind (pgBackRest exporter; backup_type incr counts full, differential and incremental backups). Alert: PgBackRestBackupStale, above obenhub.backup_age.limit (780 s in slice1). Not filtered by the instance variable: pgBackRest is its own target.

panels.title: Stanza status
panels.description: pgbackrest_stanza_status: 0 is ok, any other value is an error (1 missing stanza path and 2 no valid backups were seen live). Alert: PgBackRestStanzaError (non-zero for 2 minutes).

panels.title: Repository status
panels.description: pgbackrest_repo_status: 0 is ok, any other value is an error for that repository (the lab has repo 1). Shown only; PgBackRestStanzaError covers the same failures.

panels.title: Last backup page checksums
panels.description: pgbackrest_backup_last_error_status{backup_type="incr"}: 1 when the last backup of any kind found invalid page checksums in the data files (the backup still completes); it stays 1 while a damaged file is part of the last backup, also when later incremental backups only reference it. Alert: PgBackRestBackupChecksumError (scenario backup-checksum-error).

panels.title: PostgreSQL ERROR and FATAL (server log)
panels.description: jsonlog records read by filelog, for the selected instance.

panels.title: Delivered alert notifications

targets.expr: status:in(firing,resolved) | fields _time, status, commonLabels.alertname, commonLabels.service_instance_id, commonAnnotations.summary

panels.description: Everything Alertmanager delivered to the sink (all instances), including the Watchdog.
